subject: Phased evaluation closure, MAP milestones and uplift request
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@avasys.com>, Tim Cho <tim.cho@avasys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Proposal: phased eval -> commit milestones (MAP) and uplift guidance

Hi Lina / Tim —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Based on our conversation about production timelines and the ramp uncertainty, I sketched a phased MAP that aligns commercial triggers to milestone progress so your team can minimize upfront commitment risk while we accelerate to production. High level:

- Phase 1 (Evaluation, 4 weeks): hosted API access, up to 200k tokens/week, 24/7 support on dev incidents.
- Phase 2 (Pilot, 8 weeks): dedicated pool reservation (1 GPU pod), SLA targets, reduced per-token pricing once Phase 2 adoption metrics hit.
- Phase 3 (Ramp to Commit): commit tiers begin at month 3 based on QPS and token volumes; volume discounts and a staged uplift credit tied to successful roadmap checkpoints.

I attached a short MAP outline (MAP_Phased_Proposal_v1.pdf) with the milestone acceptance criteria and the proposed uplift schedule. Key asks from Ava Systems to close in parallel: procurement timeline, required security artifacts (SOC2 / data flow attestation), and whether you need a vendor onboarding packet for marketplace procurement.

If this looks sensible, can we lock the following calendar targets?
- Confirm MAP version + procurement checklist by Nov 9
- Pilot kick-off week of Nov 16
- Decision on commit tier by Dec 15 (this would trigger contract signature and the first month commit)

I know procurement often needs a concrete commit -> discount mapping. Marcus is looping in pricing detail in the next message. For transparency: our staged uplift is intended to protect your runway while providing predictable unit economics as usage stabilizes.

Thanks — open to a 30-min call to walk the MAP and procurement path.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0194

Attachment: MAP_Phased_Proposal_v1.pdf (7 pages, MAP milestones and pricing grid)

1) Procurement will need a clear staged commit schedule and the exact discount percentages tied to each milestone. Can you provide a table that shows: baseline price / Phase 1 price (trial) / Phase 2 pilot price / Phase 3 committed price + uplift credits?
2) We need SOC2 evidence and a brief data-retention summary for how KV cache and logs are handled during eval. Is the SOC2 excerpt you referenced available?
3) Timeline: procurement wants to review T&Cs and payor details by Nov 12 to make the pilot target Nov 16 realistic. If we can't meet that date, our internal launch will slip which tightens your year-end cadence.

Also looping Tim — our Head of Platform Ops — for the security/ops asks.

Can Marcus or someone from pricing reply with the exact numbers and a DocuSign-ready commitment template?

— Lina

Hi Lina —

Appreciate the clarity. Attaching the MAP + pricing grid and a short SOC2 excerpt per your request. Key points from the pricing table (see MAP_Phased_Proposal_v1.pdf):

- Phase 1 (Evaluation, no commit): hosted API at 0.12 / 1k tokens (trial cap 200k tokens/week) — no long-term lock and limited support.
- Phase 2 (Pilot, optional reserved pod): pilot rate 0.10 / 1k tokens while pilot active; if adoption metric A (>=10% of calls classified as production traffic) is reached within 8 weeks, price automatically steps to Phase 3 bridge rates.
- Phase 3 (Commit tiers): Monthly commit brackets (50M, 150M, 350M tokens). Each bracket reduces unit price by 10%-25% depending on bracket.
- Staged uplift credits: if you hit milestone checkpoints defined in the MAP (latency <100ms p95, developer adoption >=3 apps, production traffic >=20% of calls), we apply a one-time credit equal to 5% of the following month's invoice (applied three times across the first 3 commit months).

Procurement asks we can support now: SOC2 excerpt (attached), an example DocuSign commitment doc (we can pre-fill deal id DEV-5942), and a statement of data handling for evaluation artifacts.

I attached: MAP_Phased_Proposal_v1.pdf and SOC2_Audit_Excerpt.pdf. Naomi — if you want, I can generate the DocuSign envelope and the commitment template for procurement to review.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: MAP_Phased_Proposal_v1.pdf, SOC2_Audit_Excerpt.pdf

Marcus / Naomi — thanks for the detail. Procurement reviewed the MAP and we have two redlines before we can proceed to the Nov 16 pilot kickoff:

1) Payment term ask: Net 60 vs Redwood's standard Net 30 — procurement will accept Net 45 if we can agree to a 6% annualized surcharge during the pilot period.
2) Limit on liability: procurement requests an explicit cap tied to the pilot value (we proposed cap = 3x pilot fees).

We also need to confirm your DocuSign envelope is editable so our legal can add a short SOW addendum. Please include the DocuSign link and the envelope ID. Procurement also confirmed SOC2 excerpt is sufficient to start the pilot; they will request full report if the deal moves to commit.

If you can send the DocuSign draft and confirm Net 45 + surcharge and the liability cap language, we can approve procurement review and keep Nov 16 pilot kick-off.

On security: our ops team will run a short connectivity test week of Nov 13 — can you share an Ops contact?

Thanks,
Tim Cho
Head of Platform Ops | Ava Systems
tim.cho@avasys.com
